subject: Draft: Strategic compression & role-pairings — leadership note for QBR
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Draft: Strategic compression & role-pairings — leadership note for QBR

Team — attaching a very rough leadership note and a role-pairing matrix for the QBR cadence. High-level ask: please review and surface any blockers or framing edits by EOD Tuesday so we can finalize slides on Wednesday.

Why this change: our serving and platform teams have overlapping surface area in model rollout automation and reliability. Moving from six to four cross-functional leads (pairing product + infra for each pillar) should reduce context switching and speed decisioning during incidents and vendor negotiations.

Proposed bullets for the external-facing note (short):
- Why: reduce handoffs, speed decisions, clearer accountability for latency/cost tradeoffs
- What: compress 6 line-leads into 4 paired stewards (Prod+Infra) with clear escalation paths
- When: pilot in Q3 (90 days), review at QBR; rollback if SLAs worsen
- Impact: expected 10–20% lower decision latency; one-time reorg transition cost (2 weeks redirection)

Open questions (please flag):
- Are any teams (edge infra, dedicated ops) missing from the pairing matrix?
- Does the pilot require any SLA exceptions for Dedicated customers?
- Messaging tone: neutral+practical or aspirational?

Attachments: leadership_note_v1.docx (anchor draft), role-pairing_matrix.xlsx (mapping), qbr-one-pager.md (talking points).

Thanks — Mina
Mina Haddad
VP, Platform Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Draft: Strategic compression & role-pairings — leadership note for QBR

Thanks Mina — read through the doc. A few quick edits inline (see doc link) but top-level feedback:

- Emphasize the customer impact section earlier. Customers care about stability and commits we can honor. We should call out mitigations (fallback routing, SLA backstop).
- Pairings look reasonable but suggest one "float" engineering lead to cover cross-pillar infra spikes during launches.
- Tone: keep it pragmatic — say "pilot" and commit to metrics (decision latency, incident MTTR).

I'll add a short paragraph for the QBR slide noting expected measurement windows and escalation tests.

Jonas

Mina / team — good direction. A couple of things from an OKR lens:

- We should map the pilot to explicit OKR ticks (e.g., reduce decision latency by X%, improve deployment success rate by Y%). Without targets the pilot is hard to measure at QBR.
- Need a short rollout checklist: communications, team alignment sessions, playbook for incident handoffs. Can we add "owner" column to the matrix tying to the OKR?
- Procurement/customer side: if we compress roles we must ensure any changes don't affect existing commercial commitments — loop in Legal/RevOps for auto-exec clauses.

I'll attach a suggested OKR mapping in the spreadsheet.

Karthik

Quick notes for QBR slide pack:
- Slide 1 (one-liner + impact): keep it under 30 words, call out the pilot and measurement window.
- Slide 2 (what changes): tidy the pairing matrix into before/after columns — easier for executives.
- Slide 3 (risks & mitigations): include bullet for customer SLA backup and dedicated support hours during transition.

I can take the slide draft tomorrow AM. Also recommend we run this by Naomi in Comms for tone check before it goes to execs.

-Marissa
